info.title: Ambivo Questionnaires & KnowledgeBase API
info.description:
Core API for Ambivo Security-Q&A / RFP.

All endpoints below are served by the core API hosts listed under `servers` (ingress / vectordb); there is no separate service. Client applications are just consumers of these endpoints.

Covers the full product surface: authentication & account, users/roles/teams admin, security questionnaires + questions + answers, **knowledge-base auto-answering** and **RAG chat**, the **compliance** layer (framework-driven posture, maturity assessments, cross-framework mapping), **projects / remediation tasks / comments / notifications**, KB & file management, and **public share links ("sharecodes")** that let unauthenticated respondents fill in a questionnaire **and upload evidence files** to their answers.

## Hosts
| Host | Base URL | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| core | `https://ingress.ambivo.com` (dev `/api`) | default — `securityqa/*`, `user/*` |
| vectordb | `https://vectordbapi.ambivo.com` (dev `/vdb`) | KB RAG chat (SSE) |
| shortcode-core | `https://ingress.ambivo.com` | `entity/shortcode/*` (share links) |

Operations on the non-default hosts carry a per-operation `servers` override.

## Authentication
Most endpoints require a Bearer JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`). Pre-auth endpoints (login/register/reset) and the **public sharecode** retrieve/answer/upload endpoints take no token — for sharecodes the `{code}` (+ optional `?access_code=`) is the capability.

## The `/kh/*` namespace spans TWO hosts

`/kh/*` is the "knowledge hub" namespace and is **shared between the main API and the vectordb
service**. It is NOT a legacy alias prefix — the live crm2 client calls `/kh/*` as its primary
endpoint and selects the host per call. Build against these exact pairings:

| Path | Served by | Also reachable as |
|---|---|---|
| `kh/folders` (GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE) | **main API** | `user/folders/kb` |
| `kh/files` (GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE) | **main API** | `user/files/kb` |
| `kh/generate_answer` | **main API** | `securityqa/generate_answers` |
| `kh/chat`, `kh/get_answer` | **vectordb** | — |
| `kh/index_file`, `kh/summarize_file` | **vectordb** | — |
| `kh/file_upload_with_inference`, `kh/ocr` | **vectordb** | — |
| `pgv/*` | **vectordb** | — |

The three main-API rows are true aliases: one handler, two paths, identical contract. The vectordb
rows are NOT served by the main API at all — send them to `vectordbapi.ambivo.com` or you will get a
404.

**Historical note:** the main API also used to register `/kh/chat` locally, colliding with vectordb's
SSE chat on the same path. That alias has been removed, so `/kh/chat` now unambiguously means
vectordb. The handler behind it remains available at `user/entity/genai`.

## What a "knowledge base" actually is

A KB is NOT its own entity. It is a `file_folders` document with `folder_type == "kb"`; the `kb_name`
used by the RAG endpoints is derived server-side from the folder name via `cleanse_kb_name`.
Consequences worth knowing before building against it:

- Creating a KB means creating a folder (`user/folders/kb`, which forces `folder_type=kb`).
- Renaming or moving that folder CHANGES the derived `kb_name`, which can orphan indexed content.
- Uploading a file into a KB folder does NOT index it. Indexing is a separate per-file call
  (`user/file/index/manage`, actions `index_one` / `index_many` / `force_index`).
- A questionnaire auto-answers from the KB names listed in its `kb_proj_list`.

## Which host serves what

Operations tagged `[vectordb]` are served by the SEPARATE vectordb service
(`vectordbapi.ambivo.com`), not by the main API. They carry a per-operation `servers` override.
`POST /pgv/get_answer` is the RAG call behind `securityqa/generate_answers`; `POST /kh/ocr` extracts
text from scanned documents. You normally reach both indirectly via the main API.

## Authorization: RFP privileges (beyond "a valid token")

A valid Bearer token is necessary but NOT sufficient. Nearly every `securityqa/*` and
`securityqa/compliance/*` operation additionally carries `@rfp_privilege(...)`, granted per team:

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `C` | create |
| `R` | read |
| `U` | update |
| `D` | delete |
| `A` | **approve** — a distinct, higher level |

`A` is the one that surprises integrators: approving or unapproving an answer is checked inline
(`check_rfp_privilege(self,'A')`) and is NOT implied by `C`. A caller who can create answers can
still be refused on approve. Record-level access is resolved through team membership on the parent
questionnaire, so a token scoped to the right tenant can still be denied a specific questionnaire.

## Response envelope
Responses are **HTTP 200** even for logical errors: success = `{ "result": 1, ... }`, error = `{ "result": 2, "error_code": "...", "error": { "message": "..." } }` (login may return `result: 3` for tenant selection). **Branch on `error_code`, not the HTTP status** — the only common real non-200 is `ACCESS_CODE_INVALID` (401) on public share ops. List endpoints wrap the array under a varying key (`data` / `<resource>_list` / plural) with `total_count`/`gross_count`.

## Pagination on /securityqa/* — two modes, chosen by `action`
The same URL pages two different ways, and the mode decides which params work.
The wrong pair is accepted and IGNORED, never rejected, so the failure mode is a
plausible first page and nothing after it.

| `action` | mode | honors | emits |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get-new` | **offset** | `page_num` (1-based) + `page_size` | `gross_count` = real total, page 1 only. No `last_id`. |
| `get` (default) | **cursor** | `last_id` + `page_size` | `last_id`; `total_count` = size of the PAGE |

**Use offset (`action=get-new` + `page_num`).** All four list endpoints now
implement it; verified live Aug 2026:

| endpoint | offset works? |
|---|---|
| `securityqa/question` | YES — 48 rows / 5 pages, 0 dupes |
| `securityqa/questionnaire` | YES — 34 rows / 4 pages, 0 dupes |
| `securityqa/team` | YES — 30 rows / 3 pages, 0 dupes (since Aug 2026; the handler previously dropped `skip_num`) |
| `securityqa/answer` | YES — 48 rows / 5 pages, 0 dupes (since Aug 2026; previously had no `get-new` branch at all) |

`get` and `get-new` return byte-identical rows and field sets, so the choice is
purely about paging, never about payload.

**`total_count` is the size of the PAGE, not of the result set.** A bare request
therefore looks complete and authoritative while being truncated — a 48-question
questionnaire returned 30 questions with `total_count: 30`. Use `gross_count`
(offset mode, page 1) for a real total; never `total_count`.

**Default `page_size` is 30; the cap is 2000.** Offset: increment `page_num` from 1
and stop on a short page. Cursor: send `page_size`, take the response's `last_id`,
pass it back, and stop on a short page, an absent cursor, or a cursor that stops
advancing. No `has_more` is emitted, and none is needed.

## Conventions
Multi-action endpoints dispatch on an `action` field (modeled as one operation with an `action` enum). Optional fields are nullable; **epoch timestamps are unix seconds** and may arrive as number, numeric string, or `""`.

## Public evidence upload (sharecodes)
`POST entity/shortcode/{code}/upload` (multipart `file`, no auth) stores a file privately in the share owner's tenant and returns a `file_id`; the respondent then submits `POST entity/shortcode/{code}/answers` with `attachment_file_ids: [file_id]` on the answer. Safeguards: 25 MB/file, type allow-list, max 10 files/link.

## Related endpoints documented elsewhere

| Endpoint | Spec | Why it matters here |
|---|---|---|
| `entity/data` | `ambivo-crm.openapi.yaml` | The generic entity read used when authoring a share link: `action=picklist` backs the account/contact typeaheads, and `action=get` returns one account both for its `tags` (which pre-filter a question bank) and for the fields that prefill a per-customer link. Records come back under `data.<records-key>` (`accounts`, `account_contacts`, ...); emails live in `email_list` as `{email, type}` objects. Send `tenant_scope=true` so non-admins can populate the dropdown. |
| `user/data_import/manage` (POST only) | `ambivo-automations.openapi.yaml` | The SmartDataImportAgent view of the same import endpoint. The FULL read/update/delete surface is documented here, under the **Jobs** tag. |

## Realtime: the Tornado `/chat` WebSocket

Notifications arrive by a 60s poll of `user/notifications/manage` PLUS an optional realtime push over the Tornado `/chat` WebSocket. A WebSocket is not expressible as an OpenAPI operation, so the contract lives here (and, machine-readably, under the top-level `x-websockets` key).

To register, the client sends an `intro` frame keyed by `userid` + `connection_id`.

**`connection_id` MUST be the server-issued `client_connection_id`** - a 24-hex Mongo ObjectId returned on every login-shaped response (`user/login`, `user/get_from_token`, `admin/sms/verifications` verify, `user/mfa/verify`, `user/my_data`) and carried on `AuthUser`. The server validates it twice: it must parse as an ObjectId, AND it must match a ClientConnection record the server already minted for THAT user.

Never synthesize one client-side from a device id, user-agent or timestamp. A fabricated id is rejected, the socket never registers, and the failure is SILENT - the poll keeps working, so realtime simply never arrives while the server logs `InvalidId` on close. With no valid id, skip the socket and stay on the poll. `device_id` is a separate, free-form field and must never be reused as `connection_id`.

/chat.host: The main API host (Tornado) - not the vectordb host.

intro.description: First frame after connect; registers the socket. Rejected unless connection_id is a valid, server-minted ObjectId - see the API description.

connection_id.description: The `client_connection_id` from the login response, replayed verbatim.

device_id.description: Free-form client identifier. NOT a substitute for connection_id.

post.description: Email/password login. Resolves to one of three outcomes: authenticated (user object with token), tenant-select (result:3 with tenant_list), or an MFA challenge (no token but provider_challenge_id / mfa_required present). module_access perms arrive UPPERCASE with all:'*' and are lowercased by the client.

post.description: Pre-auth. Resolves a JWT from an OAuth redirect via the shared resolveLogin() path. Same outcomes as /user/login. Body is application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

post.description:
Pre-auth OTP endpoint. Dispatches on the action field: - send_verification_code — send an OTP to phone/email (one of
  phone_number/email is required by the backend). May return result:3
  (tenant selection needed before sending). Returns an envelope.
- verify_code — verify the OTP; returns a login envelope (authenticated /
  tenant-select / MFA). A successful verify may still return result:3.

code.description: The OTP entered by the user (required for verify_code).

phone_number.description: One of phone/email required by backend.

200.description: Envelope (send_verification_code) or login envelope (verify_code), HTTP 200 even on logical error. result:3 = tenant-selection.

post.summary: Complete or resend an MFA challenge (dispatches on action)
post.description: Pre-auth. Completes an MFA challenge from /user/login, or resends the code. When action is omitted (or not "resend") this verifies the challenge_code and returns a login envelope (normally authenticated with token). When action is "resend", resends the MFA code (the client does not inspect the response).

action.description: Set to "resend" to resend the code; omit to verify.

challenge_code.description: The MFA code from the user (required to verify).

provider_challenge_id.description: From the login MFA challenge. The challenge names the factor it was issued for, so the body carries no factor of its own.

userid.description: Owner of the challenge. The server rejects a mismatch.

200.description: Login envelope (verify) or plain envelope (resend), HTTP 200.

post.description: Pre-auth. Confirms signup with the emailed token; confirmation logs the user in (returns a login envelope). Body is application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

No request body or params.

post.summary: Create or update a tenant user
post.description:
Single upsert entry point — the handler comment is literally "for both update and
create" (user.py:13883). Distinct from the PUT on this path.

`is_superadmin` and `is_pseudo_superadmin` are stripped from the body server-side, so
privilege cannot be escalated through this call. A body that is not valid JSON raises
`InvalidPayloadException`.

parameters.description: Zero-based.

parameters.name: sort_dict
parameters.description: JSON string, always {"_id":-1}.

org_role_ids.description: Role IDs to assign (replacement set on update).

post.description:
Bearer required. Dispatches on the action body field: - create — create a role. - update — update a role; requires role_id and id (same value, sent for

get.summary: List teams or fetch one team
get.description:
Bearer required. Two modes: - List (action=get-new): paginated team list. page_num is 1-based for this
  endpoint — the client sends (page_num ?? 0) + 1 (unlike the users list,
  which is 0-based). Malformed individual team records are dropped (and
  reported), not fatal.
- Single (team_id): fetch one team; the client returns the first extracted
  item.
List payloads arrive under the first present of teams / team_list / data, with the count under total_count / gross_count / count.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description:
Read mode. The handler whitelists exactly these three; anything else returns
`INVALID_ACTION`.

- `get` (default) — cursor mode (`last_id`).
- `get-new` — offset mode (`page_num`); **this is the one to use**.
- `search` — `$text` search; **requires `search_text`**, else `SEARCH_TEXT_MISSING`.

Omit when fetching by `team_id`.

parameters.name: team_id
parameters.description: When present, fetches a single team.

parameters.name: search_text
parameters.description:
Full-text search over the collection's text index (`$text`), which matches WHOLE
WORDS with stemming — `Annu` will NOT match `Annual`.

The index was missing on this collection until Aug 2026, so every term returned
HTTP 500 (`text index required for $text query`, code 27 IndexNotFound). It now
exists and this works.

For a filter-as-you-type box prefer substring matching via
`match_filter_dict: {"name": {"$regex": "<term>", "$options": "i"}}` — that is
what the RFP UI ships. Use `search_text` when you want stemming, relevance
ranking, or to match on fields other than `name`.

Indexed fields on `team`: name, description.

parameters.name: page_num
parameters.description:
**1-based offset paging. Requires `action=get-new`** — under the default
`action=get` this endpoint uses the cursor branch and ignores `page_num`,
returning page 1 every time.

Verified live: `action=get-new` with `page_size=10` walked pages 1–3 and
returned all 30 teams with zero duplicates, terminating on an empty page.
Page 1 also carries `gross_count` (the real total).

Historical note: until Aug 2026 this param was accepted and silently
ignored in BOTH modes — the handler computed `skip_num` but omitted it
from the call into `manage_team`, so the service default of 0 always won.
Clients written against the old behaviour may still be using `last_id`.

parameters.name: last_id
parameters.description:
Cursor: the `_id` of the last row of the previous page. The response
echoes `last_id`; pass it back to advance.

Requires the default `action=get` — under `action=get-new` this endpoint
emits no `last_id` at all, so the two modes never mix. Prefer `page_num`
with `action=get-new`, which also yields a real total.

parameters.name: sort_dict
parameters.description:
JSON string. **Accepted and IGNORED** — ascending, descending and unset
all return identical order, so callers needing a specific order must sort
client-side. (`team_id` descending reproduces `{"_id":-1}`, ObjectIds being
monotonic by creation time.)

200.description: Envelope with team array under teams / team_list / data and count under total_count / gross_count / count (HTTP 200 even on logical error).

post.description: Bearer required. Creates a team (TeamInput). Each member's record_access_list defaults per role via ROLE_ACCESS_PRESETS: administrator -> c,r,u,d,a; approver -> c,r,u,a; contributor -> r,u. Response validated then discarded (void).

patch.description: Bearer required. Updates a team. userid_dict_list is a full replacement member list. Response validated then discarded (void).

delete.description: Bearer required. Deletes a team. Response validated then discarded (void).

get.description:
Two read modes on the same path:
- **List / search** — omit `questionnaire_id`. Supports paging
  (`page_size`/`last_id`/`skip_num`), full-text search (`search_text`, which also
  requires `action=search`), JSON-encoded equality filters (`match_filter_dict`,
  e.g. `{"project_id":"<id>"}`) and JSON-encoded sort (`sort_dict`). The array is
  returned under `questionnaire_list` / `questionnaires` / `data`; count under
  `total_count` / `gross_count`.
- **Single get** — pass `questionnaire_id`. The object is returned under the singular
  key `questionnaire` or as the first item in the list keys.

parameters.name: questionnaire_id
parameters.description: When set, performs a single-get of this questionnaire.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Page size (list mode). Default 30, cap 2000. Omitted if not set.

parameters.name: page_num
parameters.description:
**1-based offset paging. Requires `action=get-new`** — under the default
`action=get` this endpoint uses the cursor branch and ignores `page_num`
entirely, returning page 1 every time. That combination is the single
easiest mistake to make here.

Verified live: `action=get-new` with `page_size=10` walked pages 1–4 and
returned all 34 questionnaires with zero duplicates, terminating on a short
page. Page 1 also carries `gross_count` (the real result-set total).

Preferred over `last_id`. The server computes `skip = (page_num - 1) *
page_size` and treats 0 as "no skip", so a 0-based client silently
re-reads page one.

parameters.name: last_id
parameters.description:
Cursor paging, for the default `action=get`. The `_id` of the LAST row of
the previous page; omit it (or send empty) for the first page.

The response echoes `last_id` for the page it returned — pass that back to
advance. Walk to exhaustion: stop on a short page, an absent cursor, or a
cursor the server stops advancing (a server echoing the same cursor
forever would otherwise spin).

Prefer `page_num` + `action=get-new`, which also yields a real total.
`action=get-new` emits no `last_id`, so the two modes never mix.

parameters.name: skip_num
parameters.description:
**Accepted and IGNORED — do not use.** Verified live: `skip_num=10/20/40`
all return the FIRST page. Unlike `page_num`, it does not work under
`action=get-new` either — the handler forwards it, but only `page_num`
feeds the skip computation.

Use `page_num` with `action=get-new`.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description:
Read mode. Unlike `securityqa/question` / `securityqa/team`, this handler does
**not** whitelist `action` — it forwards whatever you send to
`manage_questionnaire`, so an unrecognised value falls through every branch and
returns the bare `{result: 2}` envelope rather than `INVALID_ACTION`. The values
below are the ones the service actually implements for reads.

- `get` (default) — cursor mode (`last_id`).
- `get-new` — offset mode (`page_num`); **this is the one to use** (see the
  pagination section in the API description).
- `search` — `$text` search; **requires `search_text`**, else `MISSING_SEARCH_TEXT`.
- `get_count` — count only.
- `get_from_marketplace` — list the curated/marketplace templates (tenant_id
  `-1`) instead of the caller's own questionnaires. Emits no `last_id`, so there
  is no cursor to walk — raise `page_size` instead.
- `get_answer_stats` — answer rollups for one `questionnaire_id`.

parameters.name: search_text
parameters.description:
Full-text search over the collection's text index (`$text`), which matches WHOLE
WORDS with stemming — `Annu` will NOT match `Annual`.

The index was missing on this collection until Aug 2026, so every term returned
HTTP 500 (`text index required for $text query`, code 27 IndexNotFound). It now
exists and this works.

For a filter-as-you-type box prefer substring matching via
`match_filter_dict: {"name": {"$regex": "<term>", "$options": "i"}}` — that is
what the RFP UI ships. Use `search_text` when you want stemming, relevance
ranking, or to match on fields other than `name`.

Indexed fields on `questionnaire`: name, description, framework, tags.

parameters.name: match_filter_dict
parameters.description:
**JSON-encoded** object of equality filters, e.g.
`{"project_id":"<id>"}` to filter by parent compliance project. Must be a JSON
string, not a nested object.

parameters.name: sort_dict
parameters.description: **JSON-encoded** sort spec (string, not nested object).

200.description: Questionnaire list or single questionnaire (or error envelope).

post.summary: Create/derive a questionnaire, or run a whole-questionnaire operation
post.description:
Multi-action write endpoint. The `action` field selects the mode:

- **add** — create an empty questionnaire from the request fields (the default
  when `action` is absent).
- **copy** — deep-copy an existing questionnaire (`questionnaire_id`) + its
  questions.
- **copy_with_answers** — like `copy`, but carries the answers across too.
- **create_from_marketplace** — instantiate a curated/marketplace template
  (`questionnaire_id` = the template). Returns the new `questionnaire_id`.
- **create_from_bank** — generate a NEW normal questionnaire from a QUESTION BANK
  (`questionnaire_id` = the bank) by cloning a FILTERED subset of its questions.
  Filter precedence: `question_ids` (manual pick / select-all) > `tags` (clone
  questions tagged GENERAL or ANY selected tag, case-insensitive) > none (whole
  bank). Optional `name` overrides the generated name. Returns the new
  questionnaire + `questions_cloned`.
- **compute_stats** — recompute and PERSIST the questionnaire's `stats_dict`
  (question count, approved %). Bulk question-add does not refresh it and the GET
  path only recomputes under a 1s timeout, so call this after a large import.
- **approve_all** — approve every approval-eligible question in one call.
- **export** — server-side export of the questionnaire + its questions.
- **publish_to_marketplace** / **delete_from_marketplace** — curate a
  questionnaire into (or out of) the shared marketplace catalog.

The handler does **not** whitelist `action`: an unrecognised value falls through
every branch and returns the bare `{result: 2}` envelope rather than a specific
`error_code`.

**Pro-gated.** `assert_pro_feature(tenant,"questionnaire")` runs before any write,
so a non-Pro tenant receives HTTP 200 with `result: 2` and
`error_code: "QUESTIONNAIRE_REQUIRES_PRO"` and nothing is created or modified.
Reads and deletes are NOT gated, so existing questionnaires stay readable on a
free plan.

createFromBankByTags.summary: Generate from a bank, filtered by tags (GENERAL always included)

createFromBankByIds.summary: Generate from a bank, explicit question pick

patch.description:
Update a questionnaire. Action `update`. Any subset of the create fields.

**Pro-gated.** `assert_pro_feature(tenant,"questionnaire")` runs before any write, so a non-Pro tenant receives HTTP 200 with `result: 2` and `error_code: "QUESTIONNAIRE_REQUIRES_PRO"` and nothing is created or modified. Reads and deletes are NOT gated, so existing questionnaires stay readable on a free plan.

200.description: Base envelope (or error envelope). No object returned.

post.summary: Generate a questionnaire from an image, PDF or raw text (LLM parsing)
post.description:
Builds a whole questionnaire — and its questions — by parsing an uploaded artefact with an LLM, instead of creating each question by hand.

The `action` selects the source:
- `generate_from_image` — parse a screenshot/photo of a questionnaire. Requires `image_url`.
- `generate_from_pdf` — parse a PDF. Requires **either** `pdf_url` (remote) **or** `pdf_path` (a path already on the server).
- `generate_from_text` — parse pasted text. Requires `text`; newline-separated, numbered lines are recognised as separate questions.

The created questionnaire is owned by the caller's tenant. `questionnaire_name` overrides the derived name; `kb_proj_list` pre-binds knowledge bases so the new questions can be auto-answered immediately via `securityqa/generate_answers`.

**Pro-gated.** Questionnaire authoring is a Pro feature — `assert_pro_feature(tenant, "questionnaire")` is evaluated before any write, so a free tenant receives the entitlement error and nothing is created.

**Cost note:** this performs LLM inference over the whole artefact and is materially slower than the plain `POST securityqa/questionnaire` create.

action.description: Which parser to run. Determines which source field is required.

image_url.description: Required for `generate_from_image`. Publicly reachable image URL.

pdf_url.description: For `generate_from_pdf`. Remote PDF URL. Mutually exclusive with `pdf_path`.

pdf_path.description: For `generate_from_pdf`. Server-side path to an already-uploaded PDF.

questionnaire_name.description: Optional name override. Otherwise derived from the parsed content.

kb_proj_list.description: Knowledge-base names to bind to the new questionnaire for auto-answering.

preview.description:
**Parse only — persist nothing.** When true the LLM's parsed structure
is handed straight back (`preview: true`, `questionnaire`, `questions`,
`sections`, `parsing_metadata`) and NO questionnaire or question is
created. Type inference is imperfect by nature, so the intended flow is
to preview, let a human correct the result, then commit through the
ordinary `POST securityqa/questionnaire` (`action: add`) + bulk
`POST securityqa/question` (bare array) endpoints.

Older builds predate this flag and IGNORE it — they create the
questionnaire outright. Distinguish the two by whether the response
echoes `preview: true` (parsed proposal) or carries a
`questionnaire_id` (already persisted); treating a persisted response
as a preview creates a duplicate on commit.

value.text:
1. Does your organization have an information security policy?
2. Are access controls implemented?

200.description:
Two shapes, both **flat** — the fields sit at the TOP LEVEL of the envelope,
not nested under `data`.

* **Persisted** (default): `questionnaire_id`, `questionnaire`, `questions`,
  `questions_created`, `parsing_metadata`.
* **Preview** (`preview: true` in the request): `preview: true`,
  `questionnaire` (name/description only), `questions`, `sections`,
  `parsing_metadata` — and no `questionnaire_id`, because nothing was written.

On a parse failure `result` is 2 and `extracted_text` is returned so the text
can be reviewed or retried by hand.

preview.description: Present and true only on a preview response (nothing was persisted).

questionnaire_id.description: Present only when the questionnaire was PERSISTED. Absent on preview.

parsing_metadata.description: `source` (image_ocr | pdf_ocr | text), `llm_provider`, `parse_method`, `total_questions_in_source`, `section_list`, and `ocr_job_id` when OCR ran.

extracted_text.description: Returned on a parse failure so the raw text can be reviewed.

get.summary: List public responses collected for a questionnaire
get.description:
Lists the submissions gathered from **collect-mode share links** for one questionnaire.

Responses are NOT answers. A respondent filling in a public sharecode writes to the separate `questionnaire_response` collection; the questionnaire's own `answer` records are untouched. That separation is what lets you send the same questionnaire to many counterparties and keep each reply distinct.

**Access:** the caller must hold team-based `r` access to the parent questionnaire (`SecurityQaService.is_accessible_to_user`). A questionnaire belonging to another tenant resolves to no-access rather than an error.

parameters.name: questionnaire_id
parameters.description: Parent questionnaire. Required — omitting it returns `MISSING_QUESTIONNAIRE_ID`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Rows per page.

get.summary: Detail of a single collected response
get.description:
Full detail of one submission collected via a collect-mode share link, including the respondent's per-question answers and any evidence files they uploaded.

**Access:** resolved through the response's parent questionnaire — the caller must hold team-based `r` access to it.

parameters.name: response_id
parameters.description: The response to fetch. Required — omitting it returns a validation error.

200.description: Envelope containing the single response document.

400.description: Validation error when `response_id` is absent or blank.

delete.description:
Permanently removes one submission collected via a collect-mode share link.

Requires team-based **`'D'` (delete)** RFP privilege on the parent questionnaire — a caller who can read responses cannot necessarily delete them. The parent questionnaire's own questions and answers are unaffected; only the `questionnaire_response` document is removed.

parameters.name: response_id
parameters.description: Response to delete.

servers.description: vectordb host — NOT the main API. This operation is served by the separate vectordb service (`vectordbapi.ambivo.com`, dev `/vdb`), not by `goferapi.ambivo.com`.

post.summary: [vectordb] RAG answer for a single question from a knowledge base
post.description:
**This endpoint lives on the vectordb service, not the main API.**

It is the retrieval-augmented-generation call that actually produces a draft answer: the KB is searched for passages relevant to `question`, and an LLM composes an answer from them.

**You normally do not call this directly.** `POST securityqa/generate_answers` is the supported entry point — it resolves which knowledge bases a questionnaire is bound to (`kb_proj_list`), calls this endpoint per question, and writes the results back as `answer` records with their citations. Call `/pgv/get_answer` yourself only when you want an answer WITHOUT persisting it.

**Auth:** same tenant Bearer JWT as the main API; the vectordb service validates it independently.

**Question type matters.** For `single-select` / `multi-select`, pass `option_list` so the model chooses among the allowed options rather than free-texting — omitting it on an option-typed question is the usual cause of an answer that cannot be mapped back to a selectable option.

kb_name.description: Knowledge base to search. Derived server-side from the KB folder name via `cleanse_kb_name` — a KB is a `file_folders` document with `folder_type == "kb"`, not its own entity.

question_type.description: Shapes the prompt. Option types should be sent with `option_list`.

additional_prompt.description: Extra instruction appended to the prompt (tone, length, house style).

streaming.description: The API sets this to `false` and reads a single JSON body. Set `true` only if you are consuming the response as a stream yourself.

200.description: Generated answer plus the source passages used. The main API maps these into `answer_text` and `answer_source_dict_list` on the persisted answer.

servers.description: vectordb host — NOT the main API. Served by the vectordb service (`vectordbapi.ambivo.com`, dev `/vdb`).

post.summary: [vectordb] Extract text from a document by OCR
post.description:
**This endpoint lives on the vectordb service, not the main API.**

Extracts text from an image or scanned PDF so the content can be indexed into a knowledge base or parsed into questionnaire questions. The main API calls it when ingesting an artefact that has no machine-readable text layer.

Backed by AWS Textract. Handles images AND scanned PDFs.
Supply exactly one source: `file_url` (any reachable URL — downloaded and processed as bytes, up to 10 MB), `s3_url` (async path, for large files), `file_path` (a path on the OCR host, uploaded to S3 first), or `bucket` + `key` (internal service calls). **Prefer `file_url`** with a presigned link from `user/file/get_url`: the `file_path` branch dereferences a tenant that can be null. Missing all four returns `result: 2` with `error: "Either s3_url, file_url, or file_path is required"`.
The route is PURE — it extracts text and writes nothing to any vector KB (embedding only happens via `persist_embeddings`, which this route never calls), so using it to parse a questionnaire does not pollute a knowledge base.

file_url.description: Any reachable URL of the document. Presigned S3 links are acceptable. Preferred source.

s3_url.description: S3 URL — selects the async Textract path, for large files.

file_path.description: Path on the OCR host; uploaded to S3 first. Supported extensions - jpg, jpeg, png, pdf, tiff, tif, bmp.

bucket.description: With `key`, forms an S3 URL. For internal/service callers.

form_document.description: Extract structured FORM data (key/value pairs) as well as raw lines — worth enabling for questionnaire layouts, which plain line extraction flattens badly.

extract_tables.description: Extract TABLE grids as well as raw lines.

streaming.description: Emit real-time progress over Redis. Requires `session_id`.

extracted_text.description: The OCR'd text. Empty string on failure.

extracted_data.description: Textract form fields / table grids, when `form_document` / `extract_tables` were set.

get.summary: List questions by questionnaire, get one, or get conditional children
get.description:
Three read modes on the same path:
- **List by questionnaire** — pass `questionnaire_id`. Array under
  `question_list` / `questions` / `data`; client sorts ascending by `seq_num`.
- **Single get** — pass `question_id`. Object under singular `question` or first list
  item.
- **Conditional children** — pass `action=get_conditional_questions` +
  `parent_question_id` (and optional `parent_answer_option_id`). Returns child
  questions that only apply when a specific parent answer option is chosen.

parameters.name: questionnaire_id
parameters.description:
List mode — questions in this questionnaire. **Paginated: this does NOT
return every question.** The default `page_size` is 30, so a 48-question
questionnaire returns 30 and looks complete (`total_count` reports 30 too,
because it is the size of the page). Page with `page_num` + `action=get-new`.

parameters.name: question_id
parameters.description: Single-get mode.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Rows per page (list mode). Default 30, capped at 2000.

parameters.name: page_num
parameters.description:
**1-based offset paging. Requires `action=get-new`** — under the default
`action=get` this endpoint uses the cursor branch and ignores `page_num`
entirely, returning page 1 every time.

Verified live: `action=get-new` with `page_size=10` walked pages 1–5 and
returned all 48 questions in seq order with zero duplicates, terminating on
a short page then an empty one. Page 1 also carries `gross_count` (the real
result-set total, 48).

Preferred over `last_id`. The server computes `skip = (page_num - 1) *
page_size` and treats 0 as "no skip", so a 0-based client silently
re-reads page one.

parameters.name: last_id
parameters.description:
Cursor paging, for the default `action=get`. The `_id` of the LAST row of
the previous page; the response echoes `last_id` for the page it returned.

Note this endpoint's cursor runs ASCENDING (`_id > last_id`), the opposite
of `securityqa/questionnaire` and `securityqa/team`, which run descending.
Prefer `page_num` + `action=get-new`.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Read mode. Anything outside this list returns `INVALID_ACTION`. `search` / `search_with_conditional_answers` require `search_text`.

parameters.name: parent_question_id
parameters.description: Required for `action=get_conditional_questions`.

parameters.name: parent_answer_option_id
parameters.description: Optional parent option that surfaces these children.

200.description: Question list or single question (or error envelope).

post.description:
Multiple actions share `POST securityqa/question`:
- **Create one** — `action=add` with question fields (object body).
- **Bulk create** — a **bare JSON array** of question-input objects (no wrapping
  `action`); the request body *is* the array.
- **Approve** — `action=approve` + `question_id`; approves the question's
  currently-approved answer.
- **Unapprove** — `action=unapprove` + `question_id`.

value.question_text: Do you encrypt data at rest?

patch.summary: Update a question, swap sequence, or move
patch.description:
Multiple actions share `PATCH securityqa/question`:
- **Update** — `action=update` + `question_id` + any subset of create fields.
- **Swap sequence** — `action=swap_seq_num` + `question_id` + `target_question_id`;
  swaps the two questions' `seq_num`.
- **Move** — `action=move_question` + `question_id` + `seq_num` (new target position).

delete.description:
Delete one or more questions. The body is `{ "question_ids": [...] }` — note **no
`action`**; always a list of ids (even for a single delete).

get.summary: List answers by question, or in bulk by questionnaire
get.description:
Two list modes. Array under `answer_list` / `answers` / `data`.

- **By question** — pass `question_id`.
- **Bulk by questionnaire** — pass `questionnaire_id`, using the denormalized
  `questionnaire_id` carried on every Answer. Returns every answer in the
  questionnaire in one call, which avoids N per-question requests (e.g. for
  PDF export).

Both modes are paginated and both support offset paging via
`action=get-new` + `page_num`. **Access scoping is identical in both paging
modes** — a non-tenant-admin without approver (`'a'`) access sees only answers
they created or updated, whichever mode is used.

Historical note: until Aug 2026 this endpoint had no `get-new` branch and
ignored `action` entirely, so `page_num` did nothing — a walk of 8 pages at
`page_size=10` returned 80 rows containing 10 unique answers. Clients written
against that behaviour may still be paging with `last_id`, which still works.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description:
Selects the paging mode. `get-new` (or `get_new`) uses offset paging
(`page_num`); anything else — including an unrecognised value — uses the
cursor (`last_id`).

Unlike `securityqa/question`, this endpoint does NOT reject unknown actions
with `INVALID_ACTION`: it has always accepted any value, and rejecting them
would break existing clients. Do not rely on that leniency in new code.

parameters.name: question_id
parameters.description: By-question mode. Exactly one of `question_id` / `questionnaire_id`.

parameters.name: questionnaire_id
parameters.description:
Bulk mode — every answer in the questionnaire. **Paginated**: the default
`page_size` is 30, so a single bare request truncates silently on any
questionnaire with more answers. Page with `page_num` + `action=get-new`.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Rows per page. Default 30, capped at 2000.

parameters.name: page_num
parameters.description:
**1-based offset paging. Requires `action=get-new`** — under the default
`action=get` this endpoint uses the cursor branch and ignores `page_num`.

Verified live: `action=get-new` with `page_size=10` walked pages 1–5 and
returned all 48 answers of a questionnaire with zero duplicates. Page 1
carries `gross_count` (the real total).

Rows are ordered `_id` descending by default — the same order the cursor
branch returns — so the two modes agree. Supply `sort_dict` to override.

parameters.name: last_id
parameters.description:
Cursor paging, for the default `action=get`. The `_id` of the LAST row of the
previous page; the response echoes `last_id` for the page it returned.

Still supported, but prefer `page_num` with `action=get-new`, which also
yields a real total. `action=get-new` emits no `last_id`, so the two modes
never mix.

post.description:
⚠️ **Known defect — do not send `is_approved: true` on create.** The approval branch of `manage_answer` never assigns `tenant_id` (the unapproved branch does), so the write fails with `required field 'tenant_id' missing`. Create the answer unapproved, then approve it via `POST securityqa/question {action:"approve"}`.

Create an answer. The body is the bare input object — **no `action` field**. The
created answer is returned under singular `answer` or as the first list item.

patch.description:
**`is_approved` cannot be changed here.** Sending a value different from the answer's current state raises `TO_UPDATE_APPROVAL_USE_QUESTION_API_WITH_APPROVE_ACTION`. Approval is a separate operation: `POST securityqa/question` with `{action:"approve", question_id, answer_id}`, which also requires the higher `'A'` (approve) RFP privilege rather than `'U'`.

Update an answer. Body requires `answer_id` plus any subset of the create fields
(no `action`). Setting `is_approved: true` approves this answer and **auto-unapproves
its sibling answers** for the same question (server-side). `comments` is appended (not
replaced). The update input uses `file_ids_list` for evidence files.

get.description:
Poll a whole-questionnaire auto-fill job. The client considers the job done when
`status === "completed"` **or** `progress >= 100`.

post.summary: Generate answers — single (sync) or whole-questionnaire (async job)
post.description:
Two modes share `POST securityqa/generate_answers`:
- **Single-question (synchronous)** — pass `question_text`. Returns drafted answers
  under `data` (array of `GeneratedAnswer`). The result is **not persisted**; no
  `job_id` is returned.
- **Whole-questionnaire (async job)** — pass `questionnaire_id`. Returns a `job_id` +
  `msg_list` to poll with `GET ?action=get_job`. `do_update="true"` (default) persists
  drafted answers; `"false"` drafts only.

value.question_text: Do you encrypt data at rest?

200.description:
Synchronous drafts (`data: GeneratedAnswer[]`) for single mode, or a submitted-job
envelope (`job_id` + `msg_list`) for questionnaire mode (or error envelope).

get.description:
List feedback records. Filters (`kb_proj_name` / `feedback_sentiment` /
`source_file_name_list`) are packed **inside** `match_filter_dict` as a JSON string,
not as separate query params. Returns `data: AnswerFeedback[]` + `gross_count`.

parameters.name: page_num
parameters.description:
1-based offset paging. **NOT confirmed live** — the probe tenant had no
feedback rows. Offset paging does work on `securityqa/question` and
`securityqa/questionnaire` (under `action=get-new`) and this endpoint
already returns `gross_count`, which is the offset-mode signature, so it is
likely to work here too. Verify before relying on it.

The server computes `skip = (page_num - 1) * page_size` and treats 0 as
"no skip", so send 1 for the first page — a 0-based client silently
re-reads page one.

parameters.name: search_text
parameters.description: Optional full-text search.

parameters.name: match_filter_dict
parameters.description:
**JSON-encoded** equality filter, built from `kb_proj_name`,
`feedback_sentiment` and `source_file_name_list` when set (omitted if all empty).

post.description:
Create a feedback record on a KB/RAG answer. Feedback is identified by answer
**text + KB + sources**, not by `question_id`/`answer_id`. Body is the bare input
object (no `action`). The created record is returned under `data`.

delete.description:
Delete one or more feedback records.

**Send the ids as QUERY PARAMS, not as a JSON body.** The handler reads its
payload with `get_request_payload`, which parses Tornado's `request.arguments` —
that covers the query string and form-encoded bodies, but NOT an
`application/json` body on a DELETE. A JSON-body call therefore finds no
`feedback_id`, raises an uncaught `KeyError` and returns **HTTP 500**, not a
`result: 2` envelope.

Supply either `feedback_id` (one id) or `feedback_ids` (a list literal, parsed
with `ast.literal_eval`). Success returns the base envelope plus `deleted` (the
number of records actually removed).

parameters.name: feedback_id
parameters.description: A single feedback record id.

parameters.name: feedback_ids
parameters.description: List literal of ids, e.g. `["fb_1","fb_2"]`. Overrides `feedback_id` when both are sent.

patch.summary: Update existing feedback on a generated answer
patch.description:
Edits feedback already recorded against a KB/RAG-generated answer — for example
changing the thumbs verdict or revising `suggested_answer_text` after review.
Routes to `manage_answer_feedback(action="update")`. Use POST to create the first
feedback record.

**The record is addressed by `id`, not `feedback_id`** (unlike DELETE, which uses
`feedback_id`), and `match_filter_dict` must be present — the service reads both
keys directly, so omitting either raises a `KeyError` the handler swallows into a
bare `{result: 2}`. Send `match_filter_dict: {}` when you have no extra filter.

Every other key in the body is `$set` onto the record verbatim, so use the stored
field names (`feedback_sentiment`, `suggested_answer_text`, …) — an invented field
is persisted as-is rather than rejected.

id.description: Feedback record to update (the `id` from the list response).

match_filter_dict.description: Extra access filter; send `{}` when unused. Required — not optional.

feedback_sentiment.description: The thumbs verdict. This is the stored field name — there is no `is_helpful`.

200.description:
Envelope with `updated` (modified count) and the refreshed record under `data`.
A no-op update (nothing changed) leaves `result: 2` and returns no `data`.

get.description:
Single GET endpoint dispatching on the `action` query param. All four
actions are GET with `action` (+ optional args) in the query string.

- `get_frameworks` — list all frameworks
  (`frameworkService.list`). No extra params. Response carries the list
  under `data` or `frameworks` (the app reads `data ?? frameworks ?? []`);
  each item is either a slug string or a framework object (see
  `Framework`); items without a resolvable identifier are dropped.
- `get_a_framework` — full definition of one framework
  (`frameworkService.get`). Requires `framework`. Response `data` is the
  framework definition (frontend treats it as `unknown`).
- `get_framework_category_codes` — the framework's control/category codes
  (`frameworkService.categoryCodes`). Requires `framework`. Response `data`
  is typically the `framework_codes_list` entries.
- `map_frameworks` — cross-map control codes from one framework to another
  (`frameworkService.map`). Requires `from_framework`, `to_framework`, and
  `from_framework_code_list` (a JSON-encoded array of control codes; the
  app sends `["*"]` when the caller passes an empty list). Legacy path —
  lowercases codes and can miss UPPERCASE data; prefer the control
  cross-reference endpoint (`/securityqa/compliance/crossref`) for a single
  control.

**An EMPTY list is reported as an ERROR, not an empty success.** A tenant with no
frameworks configured returns `{"result": 2, "data": [], "error_code": "NO_DATA_FOUND"}`
-- verified live. Per this API's own convention (branch on `error_code`, not HTTP
status) that reads as a failure, so a client that surfaces `result: 2` as an error
state will show one for the perfectly normal "nothing configured yet" case.
Treat `NO_DATA_FOUND` as an empty list.

The RFP UI is unaffected: it renders an allow-listed set of frameworks locally
rather than trusting this response.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Which framework read to perform.

parameters.name: framework
parameters.description:
Framework slug. Required for `get_a_framework` and
`get_framework_category_codes`.

parameters.name: from_framework
parameters.description: Source framework slug. Required for `map_frameworks`.

parameters.name: to_framework
parameters.description: Target framework slug. Required for `map_frameworks`.

parameters.name: from_framework_code_list
parameters.description:
JSON-encoded array of source control codes (used by `map_frameworks`).
The app sends `["*"]` (all) when the caller passes an empty list.

200.description: Success (`result: 1`) or error (`result: 2`). HTTP status is always 200.

post.description:
Resolves one control's equivalents across every other framework. Backend
path lives in the compliance module but is consumed by `framework.ts`
(`frameworkService.controlCrossref`). Case-correct (unlike `map_frameworks`).
The app keeps only `crossref` entries with a non-empty `framework` and at
least one string `code`; the response is not Zod-validated (the app
defensively coerces the shape).

Computed coverage / maturity / gap rollup for a project
(`complianceService.getPosture`). `status` values are `met` / `gap` /
`not_covered`. The app reads `.posture` and parses it with the posture
schema; throws `"Posture unavailable"` if `posture` is missing.

The frontend does **not** send `framework`, `include_controls`, or
`summary_only`, though the backend accepts them per `compliance.md`.

Builds a maturity-assessment questionnaire — one question per control in
the framework spine — whose `approved_answer_score` later feeds the posture
rollup (`complianceService.generateAssessment`). Result keys are **merged
at the top level** (no wrapper key) and parsed with the generate-result
schema.

200.description:
Success (`result: 1`) with generate-result fields merged at top level,
or error (`result: 2`).

post.summary: Assessment config (multi-action POST — get / update / delete)
post.description:
Single POST endpoint dispatching on `action`. The app reads `.assessment`
and parses it with the assessment schema; throws `"Assessment unavailable"`
if `assessment` is missing/null.

- `get` — fetch the saved assessment config
  (`complianceService.getAssessment`). Body `{ action, project_id }`.
  Returns a default config when none is saved.
- `update` — create-or-update the assessment config
  (`complianceService.updateAssessment`). Body `{ action, project_id,
  payload }` where `payload` is any subset of `AssessmentInput`.
- `delete` — documented in the backend contract (`compliance.md` §3.2) but
  **has no frontend caller**; omit unless using the backend directly.

get.description:
Rollups for the tenant dashboard (`dashboardService.basic`). The app calls
`apiRequest` with no `method` override and no params → the default verb
(GET) with an empty query. **GET only.** The handler implements no `post()` method; POST is not routed. Only
`all_questionnaires` is strictly validated; the two `*_by_*` groupings are
intentionally `unknown` (shapes vary, parsed tolerantly in
`dashboardLogic.ts`).

post.description:
Single-URL multiplexer for compliance projects, dispatched by the `action` field in the JSON body.

- **`get` (list):** send `match_filter_dict`, `page_num`, `page_size`,
  `search_text`. Returns a list of project objects wrapped under one of
  `data` / `projects` / `project_list`; count under
  `total_count` / `gross_count`. Items are validated individually;
  malformed records are dropped (and reported), not fatal.

- **`get` (single):** send `project_id` (no paging fields). Returns a
  single project under `data`; falls back to the list-extractor's first
  item. Accepted only if it parses and has a `project_id` or `id`.

- **`add`:** send `payload: ProjectInput`. Returns the base envelope; no
  body fields consumed by the frontend.

- **`update`:** send `project_id` + `payload: ProjectInput`.
- **`delete`:** send `project_id`.

Reads are enriched with rollup counts (`questionnaire_count`, `approved_questionnaire_count`, `task_count`, `open_task_count`). The frontend derives `projectApprovedPct` = `round(approved_questionnaire_count / questionnaire_count * 100)`, or `null` when `questionnaire_count` is 0.

200.description: Always HTTP 200. Success returns project data (list or single object); errors return `result: 2`.

post.description:
**Read path** for remediation tasks. Tenant-wide search filtered by `project_id` — used instead of `manage`'s `get` because the owner-scoped `get` would hide tasks assigned to other users.

Returns a **non-standard envelope**: `{ result, response: { tasks: [] } }`. The frontend also tolerates a top-level `tasks` array. Items are validated individually; non-parsing records are dropped.

A task is **open** unless `is_completed` is truthy (`true` / `"true"` / `"True"` / `1`).

200.description: Always HTTP 200. Success returns `response.tasks[]`; errors return `result: 2`.

Fans one notification out across in-app, push, websocket, email and SMS in a single
call (`UserNotificationsHandler.post`, user.py:55111). Intended for external systems,
which authenticate with a normal user auth token.

notification list. Body must be a JSON object; a non-object or unparseable body
returns `INVALID_REQUEST_BODY`.

post.summary: Create and/or launch an import job
post.description:
Multi-action write endpoint. The `action` selects the mode:

- **add** — create a job WITHOUT launching it. Set `payload.status: "draft"` to park
  it as a draft; run it later with `submit`.
- **submit** — execute an existing job by `id` (drafts, and retries of failed runs).
- **import** — shorthand for `add` + auto-launch, i.e. create and run in one call.

`payload.raw_import_list` is the parsed source rows (the caller parses the CSV/JSON,
not the server); `payload.field_mappings_dict` maps
`{targetEntityField: sourceColumnHeader}`.

`is_custom_module_entity` is **auto-detected** from `entity_type` against the
tenant's `custom_modules` collection — callers normally omit it.

Execution mode is chosen by row count: ≤30 runs synchronously, 31–3,000 defers to
Celery, >3,000 stages into 2,000-row batches. Quotas are enforced up front for
`lead` / `contact` / `account` / `questionnaire`.

A legacy `/user/import`-style body (`import_payload` at the top level instead of
`payload`) is still accepted and defaults to `auto_launch: true`.

Patch an existing job's stored fields (e.g. edit a draft's name or field mapping
before running it). `tenant_id`, `userid`, `log_type`, `ts`, `status_update_ts` and
`entity_payload_list` are stripped server-side and cannot be set.

A job in `completed` state is refused with
`CANNOT_UPDATE_JOB_IN_COMPLETED_STATE_WITHOUT_FORCE` unless `payload.force` is true.

Deletes one `data_import_log` record. Already-imported entity records are NOT

and form-encoded bodies, but NOT an `application/json` body on a DELETE. Sending
only a JSON body is a silent no-op (`result: 2`, nothing deleted).

post.description:
Public submission of questionnaire answers — **no `Authorization` header**; the `code` plus optional `access_code` authorizes. Runs the full collect gate (not-found / revoked / expired / max_accesses / access_code / IP whitelist / creator-access snapshot), plus: `entity_type` must be `questionnaire`, `questionnaire_mode == "collect"`, and the questionnaire must not be `is_locked`.

Each answer item may carry **`attachment_file_ids`** — StoredFile ids returned by the public evidence-upload endpoint (`/upload`), which link uploaded evidence to that answer (max 20/answer). An answer carrying only `attachment_file_ids` (no text/options) is still recorded. Conditional questions hidden by the respondent's own selections are soft-skipped and reported in `skipped`.

Responses are stored in the separate `questionnaire_response` collection (never the canonical `answer` collection, so approval is untouched). Each response captures `ip_address` (proxy-aware), `user_agent` (raw, ≤500 chars), and parsed `client_info` `{browser, os, device}`. If the share has `notify_on_submit`, the creator is notified via the holistic path (in-app + push + websocket + email), best-effort. The in-app/push/websocket notification is a one-line summary; the **email carries the FULL response** — a deep link to review it in the app (`/questionnaires/{questionnaire_id}?response={response_id}`), the respondent block, every question with its answer (select answers resolved to option labels, ordered by question sequence), any e-signature, and the device/IP.

**One response per link — re-submission is allowed (NOT locked after submit).** There is exactly one `questionnaire_response` per `code`: a submit promotes an existing draft in place (or inserts fresh), so re-submitting OVERWRITES the prior response and refreshes `submitted_ts`/`updated_ts`. The respondent can reopen the same link at any time until it expires, is revoked, or hits `max_accesses` (every view AND submit increments `access_count`); on reopen the retrieve returns their prior answers as `saved_response` (status `submitted`) pre-filled and still editable. There is no read-only-after-submit lock — that would be the questionnaire-level `is_locked` (a different, admin control that blocks collect entirely).

Submit-specific error codes (in addition to the shared gate codes, all HTTP 200 `result:2`): `COLLECTION_NOT_ENABLED`, `NOT_A_QUESTIONNAIRE`, `QUESTIONNAIRE_LOCKED`, `RESPONSE_LOCKED` (lock-after-submit link already submitted and not reopened), `QUESTION_NOT_IN_QUESTIONNAIRE`, `INVALID_OPTION`, `MISSING_RESPONDENT`, `NO_ANSWERS`, `SIGNATURE_REQUIRED` (when the questionnaire has `require_signature` but `signature.name`/`signature.date` are missing). `ACCESS_CODE_INVALID` returns a real HTTP 401.

If the questionnaire has `trigger_workflow_on_submit`, a successful submit also publishes a `questionnaire_response.create` event to the workflow engine (`wfapi.ambivo.com`), scoped to the owner tenant — best-effort, never affects the response.

How an unauthenticated respondent attaches evidence files to an answer. Authorized purely by the shortcode (the capability) — **no `Authorization` header**; same gate as `/answers`. Files are stored **privately in the share owner's tenant** (`make_public=False`, presigned-URL access only), tagged `source=public_shortcode` for AV/review. Upload does **not** consume the `max_accesses` budget. Owner-side retrieval uses the authed `POST /user/file/get_url` (`{file_id, create_new:false}`).

Safeguards / error codes (all HTTP 200 `result:2`): `FILE_TOO_LARGE` (>25 MB), `EMPTY_FILE` (0 bytes), `FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED` (ext must be one of pdf/png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/heic/doc/docx/xls/xlsx/ppt/pptx/csv/txt/rtf/odt/ods **and** an allowed MIME or `image/*`), `UPLOAD_LIMIT_REACHED` (per-link cap of 10 files, tracked in `shortcode_upload`), `NO_FILE` (missing field). All shared gate codes also apply; `ACCESS_CODE_INVALID` returns a real HTTP 401.

put.description:
Upsert the single DRAFT response for a collect-mode questionnaire link, keyed by `code` (one record per link). No `Authorization` header — the capability is the shortcode itself; same gate as `/answers`. Lets a respondent (or the author pre-filling) save partial progress on a long questionnaire and resume later; the public retrieve endpoint returns it as `saved_response`. A subsequent submit to `/answers` PROMOTES the draft to `submitted`.

Partial answers are allowed (empty items are skipped; conditionals are retained). Refuses to clobber an already-`submitted` response with `ALREADY_SUBMITTED` (409). Shares the `/answers` gate codes; also `INVALID_BODY`, `SERVER_ERROR` (500).

get.summary: List share links for an entity (authenticated)
get.description:
Lists the share links minted for one `entity_id` — the owner's "who did we share this with" view, and the ONLY place the internal-only fields (`recipient`, `private_note`, `shared_with`) and per-link engagement (views, response status) are readable. The public retrieve endpoint never returns these. Authenticated + tenant-scoped; non-admins see only links they created.

NOTE the hyphen: this path is registered so the public `/entity/shortcode/{code}` route (alphanumeric code) cannot capture it. Returns up to 200 links, newest first.

post.summary: Deactivate or delete share links in bulk (authenticated)
post.description:
Deactivate or hard-delete the share links for one entity — one link, several (via `codes`), or ALL (omit `codes`). Authenticated + tenant-scoped; creator-scoped for non-admins. Hyphenated path so the public `/entity/shortcode/{code}` route can't capture it.

- `deactivate` → `is_active=false`; links stop working but the records + audit trail are KEPT.
- `delete` → removes the link records + their access logs + any in-progress DRAFT responses; SUBMITTED responses are KEPT under the questionnaire.

Error codes: `INVALID_JSON` (400), `MISSING_PARAMS` (400), `BAD_ACTION` (400), `SERVER_ERROR` (500).

action.description: `deactivate`/`delete` as before. `unlock` reopens lock-after-submit links (sets `lock_released=true`) so the recipient can edit + re-submit once; `lock` re-locks immediately (`lock_released=false`). A subsequent submit auto-re-locks.

delete.description:
**DELETE is the only implemented verb** — the handler defines `async def delete(self, code)` and no `post()`. An earlier revision of this document showed POST; that never worked.

error.message: Not authorized to revoke this shortcode

CollectQuestion.description:
Question as served on a public share link. A SUBSET of `Question`: the shortcode
already identifies the questionnaire, so items carry no `questionnaire_id`, and no
tenant or audit fields are exposed publicly.

question_entry_type.description:
UI-known values: `single-select`, `multi-select`, `yes-no`, `free-text`. Backend
may return others (e.g. `files`); unknown types are treated as free-text.

primary_framework_category.description: Free-text section/category label. What the section navigator (creator detail page AND the public respond page) and PDF export group by. User-defined — NOT required to match a mapped framework; it is simply a grouping label. Persisted verbatim.

SuccessEnvelope.description: Success envelope. Returned with HTTP 200. result is always 1 on success. Additional payload keys (users / roles / teams / user / role / url / user_data / tenant_list etc.) vary per operation.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Logical-error envelope. IMPORTANT: returned with HTTP 200 (not a 4xx/5xx). The client treats result:2 as an error and rejects with this raw body.

LoginEnvelope.description: Login-style envelope. Three logical outcomes keyed by result: result:1 = authenticated (carries a user object with a token); result:3 = tenant-selection required (carries tenant_list); an MFA challenge returns result:1 with no token but provider_challenge_id / mfa_required present.

result.description: 1 = authenticated or MFA challenge; 3 = tenant-selection required.

authentication_factor_id.description: WorkOS's key for the factor, present on an SMS challenge only. An email challenge has never carried one. Address the challenge by provider_challenge_id.

AuthUser.description: Authenticated user object (authUserSchema). All fields tolerant/nullable. module_access perms arrive UPPERCASE with all:'*'; the client lowercases them. Admin flag is read from is_tenant_admin (fallback is_admin).

client_connection_id.description:
**Server-issued realtime socket id (a 24-hex Mongo ObjectId).** Minted at login
and returned on every login-shaped response (login, get_from_token, OTP verify,
MFA verify, my_data).

It MUST be replayed verbatim as `connection_id` in the `intro` frame on the
Tornado `/chat` WebSocket (see `x-websockets` in the API description). The server
validates it is an ObjectId it already minted **for this user**; anything else is
rejected, the socket never registers, and the client silently gets no realtime
push (a poll masks the failure). NEVER synthesize one client-side from a device
id, user-agent or timestamp. If it is absent, skip the socket and poll instead.

ModuleAccessMap.description: Map of module name to permission(s). Each value is a permission string or an array of permission strings. Perms from the backend are UPPERCASE with an all:'*' wildcard entry.

AdminUser.description: Tenant admin user record (adminUserSchema). All fields tolerant/nullable.

last_activity.description: Epoch unix seconds; may be a number, "" or null.

kb_name.description: The identifier the chat / generate endpoints expect.

KbFolderEnvelopeItem.description: A folder list entry. Often wrapped under a singular `folder` key; the client unwraps it. May also appear as a bare string (name-only) in the name picker.

KbFile.description: A KB file entry. Parsed tolerantly (the list may wrap items under a `file` key).

entity_type.description: `questionnaire`, `file`, `folder`, a standard CRM type (lead/contact/account/...), `dashboard`, `kh_workspace`, or a custom collection name.

entity_id.description: The record id. Required unless `match_filter_dict` is provided (single-record mode).

match_filter_dict.description: Filter criteria for multi-record (filter) mode. Mutually exclusive with `entity_id`.

questionnaire_mode.description: For questionnaires: `collect` enables the public answer/upload endpoints; `review` (default) is read-only.

access_code.description: 6-char alphanumeric code (stored/compared uppercase). Null/omitted = no protection.

notify_on_submit.description: Notify the share creator on each response (collect mode). Delivered on the holistic path: a one-line in-app/push/websocket summary PLUS an email containing the full response (a deep link to review it in the app, respondent, every question + answer, e-signature, device/IP). Best-effort — never fails the respondent's submit.

whitelist_ips.description: Allowed IPs/CIDR ranges. Null/empty = all IPs allowed.

shared_with.description: INTERNAL ONLY — free-text note of who the link went to. Stored on the shortcode, never echoed by the public retrieve endpoint.

private_note.description: INTERNAL ONLY — private commentary about this link. Never shown to the recipient.

send_email.description: Email the link to `recipient.email` from the author's connected mailbox. Best-effort; never fails link creation. Explicit opt-in — off by default. When the link is access-code protected, the email adds a fine-print line ("If an access code is required, it will be sent to you separately.") and never carries the code itself.

share_message.description: Optional personal note included in the invitation email (only used when `send_email`).

heading.description: PUBLIC per-link presentation (unlike shared_with/private_note/recipient, which are internal-only). Heading shown atop the respondent page; when blank NO product/brand name is shown (only the questionnaire name + owner branding, if any). Echoed on retrieve as `shortcode_info.heading`.

copyright.description: PUBLIC per-link copyright/footer line appended to the respondent page footer (takes precedence over the auto owner-tenant copyright). Echoed on retrieve as `shortcode_info.copyright`.

lock_after_submit.description: Collect mode. When true, the link goes READ-ONLY once a response is submitted: the respondent can no longer edit/re-submit (submit + upload return `RESPONSE_LOCKED`, retrieve sets `data.locked=true`) until the owner reopens it (bulk-manage `unlock`). A subsequent submit auto-re-locks, so each reopen grants exactly one edit.

create_instance.description: `questionnaire` only. When true (or when `prefix_questions` is non-empty), the backend CLONES the questionnaire into a hidden, frozen per-link instance (its own id) and repoints this link at the clone, so each customer's answers live on a separate record. The instance is excluded from the main questionnaire list but reachable by direct id. On clone failure the original questionnaire is shared instead.

prefix_questions.description: `questionnaire` only, requires instancing. Up to 10 questions PREPENDED to the instance (seq 0..m-1). Where a `prefilled_answer` is set it is seeded as a draft response (keyed by the shortcode `code`) so the customer sees it already filled in (still editable). The seed is returned on retrieve as `data.saved_response` (see `GET /entity/shortcode/{code}`). Authors typically source these values from the target CRM `account` (company name, employees, revenue, industry, primary email), pairing this with `recipient.account_id`.

ShareRecipient.description: Structured, author-supplied recipient for a per-customer link. Internal-only (never in the public allow-list). Pre-fills the respondent and optionally emails the link.

account_id.description: CRM account this link went to (linkage lives on the LINK, not the questionnaire).

PrefixQuestion.description: A pre-filled question authored at share time and prepended to the per-customer instance.

options.description: Options for select types. Each carries `answer_text` (+ optional `answer_score`); backend mints fresh `option_id`s.

prefilled_answer.description: Author-set answer, seeded onto the instance as a draft (editable by the customer).

public_url.description: Canonical, backend-resolved share link (correct host for the entity type). Prefer this.

email_sent.description:
True when the invitation email was successfully handed to a transport
(`send_email: true` plus a `recipient.email`). Best-effort and non-fatal — a
failed send still returns `result: 1` with `email_sent: false`, so surface it
rather than assuming the recipient was notified.

ShareRecord.description: One share link as listed for the owning tenant (never for a recipient). Includes the internal-only recipient/notes and per-link engagement.

entity_id.description: The questionnaire this link points at — a hidden instance clone when instanced.

is_instance_share.description: True when `entity_id` is a per-customer instance clone.

parent_entity_id.description: The template the instance was cloned from (only when `is_instance_share`).

view_count.description: Durable per-link view analytics (distinct from access_count).

lock_after_submit.description: Whether this link locks to read-only after submit.

lock_released.description: Owner has reopened the link for one more edit (see bulk-manage `unlock`).

is_edit_locked.description: Derived effective state — true when `lock_after_submit` and a response was submitted and not currently released. The UI shows a Locked badge + a Reopen action.

public_url.description: Canonical share link, so a viewer can redirect to the correct host.

heading.description: Optional per-link heading set at share time (empty when unset). Shown atop the public respondent page; blank means no product/brand name is shown.

copyright.description: Optional per-link copyright/footer line set at share time (empty when unset). Appended to the public page footer.

RetrievePayload.description: The `data` object. Its shape varies by entity type — for a collect questionnaire it carries `questionnaire` + `questions`; other types carry file metadata, folder children, or filter-mode `records`.

branding.description: Owner-tenant branding for the public header — present only when the questionnaire has `show_branding`.

saved_response.description: A previously-saved draft (or prior submission) for THIS link, returned so the respondent can resume — and the vehicle for PRE-FILL. When the link was created with `prefix_questions` carrying `prefilled_answer`s (and/or a `recipient`), the backend seeds a draft keyed by the shortcode; it comes back here with the respondent pre-populated and one `items` entry per pre-filled question, so the recipient opens the form already partly answered. `null` when no draft/submission exists yet.

locked.description: Lock-after-submit state — true when this link was submitted and locked and the owner has not reopened it. The respond page renders VIEW-ONLY (inputs disabled, no submit) in this state. Absent/false otherwise.

SavedResponse.description: The draft (or prior submission) for a single share link, returned under `data.saved_response` on retrieve. Powers resume-later AND the pre-filled experience: for a link created with `prefix_questions`/`recipient`, this is the seeded draft the recipient sees on first open. One record per link.

status.description: `draft` while in progress (incl. a pre-fill seed); `submitted` once the respondent has submitted.

respondent.description: Pre-populated respondent identity (from the share `recipient`, when supplied).

items.description: One entry per answered/pre-filled question. Free-text / yes-no carry `answer_text`; select types carry `selected_question_option_ids`. `question_id` matches the (cloned) instance's question ids.

updated_ts.description: Epoch seconds of the last draft save (or seed).

submitted_ts.description: Epoch seconds of submission; null while still a draft.

phone.description: Optional. Captured for the owner + any triggered workflow.

contact_id.description: Optional, if the share was targeted at a known CRM contact.

Signature.description: Respondent electronic signature (affidavit). Required on submit when the questionnaire has `require_signature`, otherwise optional.

AnswerSubmitItem.description: One answer. Route by shape: select types use `selected_question_option_ids`; free-text / yes-no use `answer_text`. `attachment_file_ids` links evidence uploaded via `/upload` (≤20/answer); an item carrying only `attachment_file_ids` is still recorded.

attachment_file_ids.description: StoredFile ids from the public evidence-upload endpoint (`/upload`).

access_code.description: May be supplied here instead of the query param (query param preferred).
